recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. Handle any future changes to DeviceAssociation subject scope, relationship semantics, or search parameters in separate DeviceAssociation-specific trackers rather than reopening FHIR-39009.
issue_request: FHIR-39009 was a Published, Not Persuasive with Modification R5 Device issue asking to resolve conflicting prior Device subject trackers by adding Practitioner and RelatedPerson to Device.association.humanSubject and by supporting non-human Device subjects. Its final resolution was to link to the FHIR-38904 disposition.
initial_application: No direct FHIR-39009 source commit was found. The relevant application came through FHIR-38904: commit 620b8fa10c746066887014813e72cf08475a42c0 introduced DeviceAssociation with DeviceAssociation.subject references to Patient, Group, Practitioner, RelatedPerson, and Device, and commit 7a135eb3489ef36b8935e36d80d88b1729a2e8e8 recorded FHIR-38904 QA follow-up. Earlier FHIR-32570 commits had moved Device.subject into Device.association, but FHIR-38904 later superseded that placement.
additional_context: FHIR-38904 directed creation of DeviceAssociation, removal of the Device.association backbone from Device, and a subject reference set including Patient, Group, Practitioner, RelatedPerson, and Device. OO WGM minutes recorded acceptance of that disposition with an 8-0-2 vote. Current source has DeviceAssociation active in fhir.ini, active subject/patient search parameters on DeviceAssociation.subject, and narrative examples for Practitioner, Device, and RelatedPerson. The old Device.association.humanSubject and Device subject/patient search parameters are only XML comments.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current built specification already reflects the FHIR-39009 resolution through active DeviceAssociation source; changing the commented-out Device.association.humanSubject block would not affect the built spec and would conflict with the FHIR-38904 decision to move patient-identifying association data out of Device.
